quests.instruction: Mum scolded Ravi for leaving his bike in the road. Later, when he fell and scraped his knee, she knelt down to…
quests.hint: What does a parent do for a child who is hurt?
quests.explanation: To scold is to tell someone off. To comfort is to soothe them and make them feel better.
quests.funFact: “Comfort” comes from Latin words meaning “with strength”.

quests.instruction: “Don’t mix the picture books with the novels,” said the librarian. She wants them kept…
quests.hint: Things kept apart are not mixed.
quests.explanation: To mix is to put things together. Keeping things separate keeps them apart in their own groups.
quests.funFact: Many libraries sort books using systems such as the Dewey Decimal system.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that means the opposite of “Ben locked his bike to the rack”.
quests.correctAnswer: Ben unlocked his bike from the rack.
options: Ben parked his bike by the rack.
Ben unlocked his bike from the rack.
Ben painted his bike near the rack.
quests.hint: Which action frees the bike again?
quests.explanation: Locking secures something; unlocking frees it. “Parked” and “painted” don’t reverse the locking.
quests.funFact: The first bicycle locks were simple chains.

quests.instruction: Straight from a new bottle, the soda was fizzy. After two days with the cap off, it tasted…
quests.hint: What escapes from a drink left open?
quests.explanation: Fizzy drinks are full of bubbles. When the bubbles have escaped, the drink goes flat.
quests.funFact: The bubbles in fizzy drinks are made of carbon dioxide gas.

quests.instruction: Complete the opposite idea: “Kofi borrowed a pen, so Ana ___ him a pen.”
quests.hint: One person gave the pen and the other took it.
quests.explanation: Borrowing and lending are two sides of the same action. Ana lent the pen and Kofi borrowed it.
quests.funFact: “Loan” is related to the word “lend”.

quests.instruction: In a line dance, the dancer at the front leads the steps. The dancers behind copy and…
quests.hint: Think of the dancers behind the leader.
quests.explanation: Leading means going first and showing the way. Following means doing as the leader does.
quests.funFact: Many folk dances around the world are danced in lines or circles.

quests.instruction: A ripe orange squirts juice when you squeeze it. One forgotten on the shelf for weeks feels hard and…
quests.hint: What happens to the inside of fruit that’s left too long?
quests.explanation: Juicy fruit is full of liquid. Dry fruit has lost it.
quests.funFact: Oranges are mostly water.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the opposite of “The bananas are ripe and sweet”?
quests.correctAnswer: The bananas are green and hard, not ready yet.
options: The bananas are green and hard, not ready yet.
The bananas are cheap and plentiful.
The bananas are long and curved.
quests.hint: Picture bananas that aren’t ready to eat.
quests.explanation: Ripe fruit is ready to eat. The opposite is fruit that’s still green and needs more time.
quests.funFact: Bananas are picked green and ripen on the way to the shops.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence: “The fox in the forest is wild, but the ___ cat on the sofa lets everyone stroke it.”
quests.hint: Which animal lives with people?
quests.explanation: Wild animals live free and avoid people. Tame animals are used to being around them.
quests.funFact: Dogs are descended from wolves.

quests.instruction: For the wedding, Raj wore a suit and tie, which is formal. For a Saturday cricket game with friends, he wore jeans and an old T-shirt, which is…
quests.hint: Which outfit would you wear to play, not to dress up?
quests.explanation: Formal clothes are for special or serious events. Casual clothes are relaxed and comfortable.
quests.funFact: “Casual” comes from a Latin word meaning “chance”.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence with the opposite meaning: “Please use the entrance on the left.”
quests.correctAnswer: Please use the exit on the left.
options: Please use the stairs on the left.
Please use the exit on the left.
quests.hint: Change one word to turn “way in” into “way out”.
quests.explanation: An entrance is a way in. An exit is a way out.
quests.funFact: Many theatres have glowing exit signs so people can find their way in the dark.

quests.instruction: Which sentence means the opposite of “Ria put on her coat before stepping out”?
quests.correctAnswer: Ria took off her coat after coming in.
options: Ria buttoned her coat before stepping out.
Ria took off her coat after coming in.
Ria put on her hat after coming in.
quests.hint: Think of what you do with a coat once you’re warm indoors.
quests.explanation: Putting on adds clothing; taking off removes it. The time flips too: before going out becomes after coming in.
quests.funFact: The word “coat” has been used in English for about 700 years.

quests.instruction: Zubin pulled his sweater over his head and noticed the seams on the outside, so it was on inside out. Turning it the proper way means putting it…
quests.hint: Which side should the seams be on?
quests.explanation: Inside out shows the inner seams. Right side out puts the finished side where it should be.
quests.funFact: Many clothes have a tag stitched inside, which helps you tell the back from the front.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence: “The puddle will shrink in the sun, while the pumpkin in the garden will…”
quests.hint: The pumpkin does the opposite of the puddle.
quests.explanation: Shrinking means getting smaller, and growing means getting bigger.
quests.funFact: Some giant pumpkins weigh over a tonne.

quests.instruction: Which sentence has the opposite action to “Anil sent a message to his friend”?
quests.hint: Every sent message has someone waiting on the other end.
quests.explanation: Sending and receiving are opposite ends of the same message.
quests.funFact: The first email was sent in the early 1970s.

quests.instruction: Under the mango tree, the ground stayed cool in the ___, while the open playground baked in the sunshine.
quests.hint: Where do you stand to get out of the sun?
quests.explanation: Sunshine is direct sunlight. Shade is the cooler place where something blocks it.
quests.funFact: Shade can be several degrees cooler than direct sun.

quests.instruction: Complete the instruction: “Write your name on the board, then ___ it before the next class.”
quests.hint: Think of the action that takes writing off a whiteboard.
quests.explanation: Writing leaves marks; erasing removes them.
quests.funFact: Rubber erasers were first used in the 1700s to rub out pencil marks.

quests.instruction: Which sentence means the opposite of “Add 5 and 3”?
quests.hint: Start from 8 and work backward.
quests.explanation: Subtraction undoes addition. Starting from 8 and taking away 3 gets you back to 5.
quests.funFact: Addition and subtraction are called inverse operations because one undoes the other.

quests.instruction: On a one-way street, cars may only go one direction. On a two-way street, traffic moves in…
quests.hint: How many ways can cars travel on the road?
quests.explanation: One-way means traffic goes one way only. Two-way means it travels in both directions.
quests.funFact: One-way streets can help traffic flow more smoothly in busy city centers.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the opposite action: “Mira threw the ball high, and Tej ran forward to ___ it.”
quests.hint: A fielder’s hands are ready under a high ball.
quests.explanation: Throwing sends a ball away. Catching brings it in.
quests.funFact: Baseball players wear a glove to help them catch the ball.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the opposite of “The captain raised the flag”?
quests.hint: Watch which way the flag goes at the end of the day.
quests.explanation: Raising lifts something up; lowering brings it down.
quests.funFact: Flags have been used at sea for hundreds of years to send signals.

quests.instruction: The car accelerated away from the traffic light. Seeing a child step into the road, the driver quickly pressed the…
quests.hint: Which pedal makes the car stop?
quests.explanation: Accelerating makes a vehicle go faster. Braking slows it down or stops it.
quests.funFact: Many modern cars have automatic emergency braking.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence with the opposite meaning: “The children gathered around the storyteller.”
quests.correctAnswer: The children scattered across the playground.
options: The children clapped for the storyteller.
The children sat around the storyteller.
The children scattered across the playground.
quests.hint: Picture children moving away from the storyteller.
quests.explanation: Gathering brings people to one spot; scattering spreads them out.
quests.funFact: Storytelling is one of the oldest forms of entertainment.

quests.instruction: Which sentence has the opposite meaning: “Tara ate the whole sandwich.”?
quests.correctAnswer: Tara ate half of the sandwich.
options: Tara ate half of the sandwich.
quests.hint: Check which sentence changes how much she ate.
quests.explanation: Whole means all of it. Half means only a part. The other choices change speed or place.
quests.funFact: The sandwich is named after the Earl of Sandwich, an English nobleman from the 1700s.

quests.instruction: In the reading corner, Maya read the poem aloud for the class. Afterward, everyone read it again, this time…
quests.hint: How do you read a poem without making any sound?
quests.explanation: Reading aloud uses your voice. Reading silently happens only in your head.
quests.funFact: When you read silently, your eyes usually move faster than when you read out loud.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the opposite of “The ice cream began to melt in the sun”?
quests.correctAnswer: The juice began to freeze in the freezer.
options: The juice began to boil on the stove.
The ice cream began to drip in the sun.
The juice began to freeze in the freezer.
quests.hint: Think of liquid turning hard in the freezer.
quests.explanation: Melting turns solid into liquid. Freezing turns liquid into solid.
quests.funFact: Water freezes at 0°C and melts at the same temperature.

quests.instruction: A dog keeps its body temperature steady in any weather, so it’s warm-blooded. A lizard warms itself by lying in the sun, so it’s…
quests.hint: Where does a lizard get its heat from?
quests.explanation: Warm-blooded animals make their own body heat. Cold-blooded animals depend on the outside temperature.
quests.funFact: Lizards bask on sunny rocks to warm up.

quests.instruction: Before the toy train can run, you have to wind it up. After a long school week, Dad likes to…
quests.hint: What do you do to relax after a busy week?
quests.explanation: Winding up tightens a spring or a mind. Unwinding loosens it, and it also means to relax.
quests.funFact: Clockwork toys store energy in a coiled spring as you wind them.

quests.instruction: The doctor said, “Please lie down on the bed.” After the check-up, she said, “You can now…”
quests.hint: Think of the moment the check-up is over.
quests.explanation: Lying down puts your body flat. Standing up brings you upright.
quests.funFact: Doctors often ask patients to lie down so they can examine the stomach more easily.

quests.instruction: Which sentence means the opposite of “The audience entered the hall”?
options: The audience sat in the hall.
The audience clapped in the hall.
quests.hint: Picture people streaming out through the doors.
quests.explanation: Entering is going in, and leaving is going out.
quests.funFact: Concert halls are often built with curved walls to help the sound reach every seat.
